thread:
marta: Quick question — how should the gateway handle retries for long-running streaming responses when we need to re-route mid-stream because an upstream is scaling down? Right now we either abort or restart from scratch; both are awful for latency and cost. Thoughts on a 'soft-handoff' / resume token approach?

alex: I'm +1 on trying to avoid full restarts, but big caveat: side-effects and non-idempotent streams. We should limit anything resumable to idempotent or pure-output paths. Also worried about memory and attack surface if we store checkpoints.

sam: Proposed sketch: upstream emits periodic lightweight checkpoints (opaque blobs) as part of trailers or inline events. Gateway stores an encrypted handle (no plain blob on disk) with short TTL, and if we need to re-route we try to replay the last checkpoint to a warm upstream instance. Not perfect resume, but prefix caching reduces wasted tokens. Example headers/payload:
```
X-RW-Resume-ID: rsm_abc123
X-RW-Checkpoint: base64(eyJvZmZzZXQiOjEwMiwicHJvZ3Jlc3MiOiJhbHkifQ==)  # opaque to gateway
```

marta: That matches what I was imagining. A few operational constraints: 1) checkpoint TTL should be short (30s-2m) to bound memory; 2) encryption via KMS and only handles circulate outside R/W; 3) trace propagation must carry resume-id so tracing and billing tie back correctly.

ops-bot: Deploy note: the resume prototype branch landed to staging earlier today (deploy #2026.03.23-rc3). Observability flag `edge.resume_prototype` is off by default.

leo: Security / privacy note: checkpoints might contain model context or PII depending on the app. We need a classification step upstream that indicates "checkpoint-safe" or not. If not safe, no resume. Also must surface policy in the API (opt-in).

alex: UX choices: do we expose resume through client-visible headers (X-RW-Resume-ID) or via trailers? Trailers are conceptually correct but have spotty client support; headers are easier but coupling to initial request. If header, clients can re-request with `Resume-ID` to hint the gateway.

sam: Implementation plan idea (small incremental):
- phase 1: add checkpoint emission support in runtime for idempotent routes + gateway in-memory handles (TTL=30s)
- phase 2: add encrypted persistent handles for longer windows behind feature flag (TTL configurable)
- phase 3: surface metrics: resume_attempts, resume_successes, resume_fallbacks, resume_latency_savings

marta: Agreed. Decision heuristics we need in RFC: what counts as checkpoint-safe, max storage per tenant, per-request retry budget interaction, and how to fall back (send partial + `X-RW-Partial: true` if resume fails). Also need an opt-out header for customers who don't want any resume artifacts.

alex: One more tradeoff: resuming can mask upstream failures and skew SLO accounting. We should mark resumed responses in billing/telemetry so we can attribute cost correctly.

marta: I'll draft a short RFC capturing interface, security checklist, telemetry hooks, and a minimal prototype plan. I'll tag @eng-runtime, @eng-security, and @product. If anyone objects to the overall soft-handoff approach, please say now. Otherwise I'll open the RFC this afternoon. :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup: capturing a few metrics will make this easy to evaluate. Also recommend a boolean `Resume-Accepted: true|false` trailer so clients can know whether their hint resulted in a resume.

leo: Agree. I'll add security review items once the RFC is up.

marta: Thanks — RFC will link to staging deploy and telemetry dashboard. Next: I'll create the draft and ping here when it's ready.
